headline: Gemini is coming to your Mac to do stuff for you
summary: Only one thing worth a look today: the Gemini Mac app can now work your computer for you.

items.title: Gemini Mac app can control your computer
items.pitch: Google's Josh Woodward announced that the Gemini Mac app can now do tasks right on your computer, and said it was the most requested feature.
why: No coding needed, so non-developers can get AI to click the mouse for them
Repetitive work tasks might get handed straight to it
It goes head to head with Claude's and Codex's computer-control features
actions: Update or download the Gemini Mac app and look for the new task feature
Try it on small stuff without sensitive data first, like organizing files
deep_dive: The only source is this one tweet, with no details. It's still unclear what tasks it can do, whether it's free or paid, or if it needs a specific subscription.
Before installing it on a work computer, check that your IT policy lets AI control the screen. Keep it away from salary data.
items.signals: Josh Woodward tweet 876 likes · 35 retweets · just one tweet, not enough detail

items.title: Big ChatGPT mobile redesign
items.pitch: Thibault Sottiaux from the Codex team says they're building a new ChatGPT mobile interface, starting with some Pro users.
why: You can pin Codex, Projects, and Images to the bottom bar
You can turn it on or off anytime, no forced switch
items.signals: Thibault Sottiaux tweet 5244 likes · 276 retweets · another one mentions 1.2 billion users

still_tracking.name: Gemini 4 Neon
still_tracking.update: After comparing it with Opus 5.5, Peter Yang said he'll use Neon for 99% of his tasks, and that its writing and personality hold up fine. Simon Willison complained that the pricing is confusing, and Neon is the priciest right now.
